newsitem.title: UK: FTSE 100 ends firmer, second straight closing high.
newsitem.headline: FTSE 100 ends firmer, second straight closing high.

text.p: Leading UK shares ended a dull session firmer on Monday, marking a second consecutive closing high, but trading volume was thin with many dealing rooms half-empty ahead of the Christmas holiday, traders said.
The FTSE 100 added 9.6 points to settle at 4,087.2, the day's high, on turnover of only 452.5 million shares.
"We saw a bit of business this morning, some year-end book squaring...but there's no great trend. The market is dying a slow death," said one broker.
"In the end, we believe sales will prove to be quite strong," said one market maker.
Shares in Marks & Spencer added 7p to 479-1/2p.

Yorkshire Electricity, one of only two remaining independent regional electricity companies (RECs), saw its shares surge 25-1/2p to 798p amid speculation that it would be the next REC to succumb to a takeover bid.

Elsewhere in the sector, Northern Electric shares were suspended at the company's request after the UK takeover panel said the electricity concern would appeal against its decision to extend the deadline on the bid from CalEnergy.
CE said it had acceptances for 50.13 percent of Northern shares.
Shares in British Aerospace rose 16-1/2p to 1225-1/2p stake, would become a stock company by 1999, market makers said.
An official of Daimler-Benz Aerospace Airbus, one of BAe's partners in Airbus, told a German newspaper that the move to a stock-holding company was planned for before 1999.
